subject: Request: Meridian POC - SLA tiers + adaptive batching exemption (deal timing)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Meridian POC - ask to Product: SLA tiers + adaptive batching exemption

Sooj,

Quick one — Meridian Bank (Alice Turner) is ready to sign a 12-month Dedicated commit but they need two items in the POC to land this quarter:

1) Opt-in SLA tiers for the pilot (ability to set tenant-level latency SLOs and a soft-fallback policy)
2) An "adaptive batching exemption" for a single tenant during the POC window to ensure sub-100ms p95 for conversational flows

They want confirmation by EOD Friday so procurement can move the PO. Terms: 20% uplift on ARR if we can deliver the POC behaviors and security attestation. If Product/Eng can commit to a scoped shim and ETA (~3 weeks), Sales will accept a 30-day conditional holdback (SOW clause) rather than pushing for immediate GA-grade work.

Attached: Meridian_MAP_v1.xlsx (mutual action plan), SOW_draft.pdf. Also forwarded their security questionnaire (email from security@meridianbank.com) — they flagged caching and per-tenant KV retention as concerns.

Ask: Can Eng scope a limited, reversible config-path that bypasses global batching for the Meridian tenant and expose SLA tier flags (no UI required — API + env) OR give us a clear no with the technical blocker so we can negotiate the offer?

Ben
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Thanks Ben — looping in Product/Eng formally.

Dylan / Dev: summary of asks from Sales/CS and Meridian (copied above):
- Tenant-scoped SLA tiers (config flag to reduce queueing/batching and opt into lower-latency path)
- Tenant-level adaptive batching exemption/override for the POC window (reversible, feature-flagged)

Constraints/priorities to consider: this is a high-dollar Strategic POC (MER-2027-019). Sales is proposing a time-boxed shim in exchange for a significant ARR uplift if the POC signs. Marissa: can you confirm the expected traffic profile for the POC (qps, avg seq len)? I want to ensure we scope perf correctly.

Please reply with: 1) Feasibility (yes/no/partial), 2) High-level design approach, 3) Rough ETA (days/weeks), and 4) Any compliance/security blockers. If we can provide an owner and a minimal test plan, Sales will push for Friday confirmation.

—Soojin

Sooj / team — quick numbers from pre-sales: expected peak qps ~40 for a 1-hour heavy window, steady-state 6-8 qps. Typical sequence lengths 80-150 tokens. Latency requirement: p95 < 100ms for the critical conversational route.

Customer is comfortable with a POC-only config that disables batching for the tenant and grants a short-lived route that pins the model instance (they're fine with increased cost for the POC). They've also asked for confirmation on KV TTL controls (they want 24h retention guarantees and an audit trail). Security flagged the questionnaire — I've attached the filled questionnaire (Meridian_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx) to the forward they sent earlier.

Marissa
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Meridian POC - ask to Product: SLA tiers + adaptive batching exemption

Team — thanks for the context. Quick technical read:

1) Batching exemption: feasible as a short-term shim. Implementation options:
   - Per-tenant runtime flag that tags requests to bypass the central batching queue and route to a dedicated warm pool (fast, reversible) — estimated 8-12 engineer days for a small oncall pair to implement, test, and document.
   - Alternatively, prioritize the tenant's requests in the existing batcher (less invasive) but that does not guarantee the hard p95 <100ms at peak.

2) Tenant SLA tiers: exposing a config flag + API surface to define service class is straightforward (3-5 days) but enforcement requires runtime work and monitoring + alerting (additional 5 days).

3) KV TTL and audit: we can add per-tenant TTL enforcement quickly (2-3 days) if storage supports it; audit trail requires adding a retention log entry (2 days).

Blockers / notes:
- We need a dedicated warm pool for the POC if we want consistent p95 under load; that increases infra cost for the pilot and needs billing approval.
- Any change that bypasses batching must be reversible and feature-flagged with a kill-switch before customer rollout.

Proposed minimal scope (to hit Friday commitment):
- Implement per-tenant runtime flag + route to warm pool (8-12d)
- Add per-tenant TTL enforcement (2d)
- Deliver a test plan and smoke harness for the customer (2d)

Can we agree on a 3-week delivery horizon if we prioritize this immediately? If Sales needs <7 days, we can do an MVP (priority in batcher + TTL + test plan) but cannot promise consistent p95 <100ms at peak.

—Dev
Senior SRE Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Aug 2027 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Meridian POC - ask to Product: SLA tiers + adaptive batching exemption

Appreciate the quick turn. Decision and next steps:

1) We will proceed with the scoped, timeboxed shim: per-tenant runtime flag + dedicated warm pool routing + per-tenant TTL enforcement. This is the 3-week track (owner: Dev, primary engineer: TBD).

2) Constraints accepted by Sales/CS: initial rollout is POC-only, feature-flagged, and will incur an infra uplift that Sales will document in the SOW. Product will not consider this GA work until we validate in production; any follow-on requests will go through normal prioritization.

3) Requirements before work starts:
   - Marissa to provide a signed mutual action plan and final SOW clause by Monday EOD (Meridian commits to pilot dates).
   - Ben to get procurement acknowledgement of the cost uplift and confirm the holdback clause (we require the 30-day conditional holdback as negotiated).
   - Dev to prepare a test plan, rollout kill-switch, and a perf acceptance test script for Meridian.

If everyone confirms, I'll create an internal ticket and mark this as "expedite" for the 3-week sprint. This will be a one-off tactical acceleration; Product expects a short retro after the pilot.

Thanks — I'll send the ticket and timeline when we have the SOW/MAP.

—Soojin
Senior Manager, Product Strategy | Redwood Inference
